title: After Twenty Years

teacherSummary.text: A man waits in a New York doorway to meet his old friend Jimmy Wells, twenty years to the day after they parted. He tells a patrolling policeman about the plan. A man claiming to be Jimmy arrives, but he is a plainclothes officer who arrests the waiting man, 'Silky' Bob, wanted in Chicago. A note reveals that the patrolman was Jimmy, who recognized Bob as the wanted man and could not arrest him himself.

I read “Twenty years is a long time, but not long enough to change a man’s nose from a Roman to a pug” slowly and put it in my own words: Under the drug-store lights, Bob himself snaps that twenty years is not long enough to change a man's nose from a Roman to a pug, so the tall man beside him cannot be Jimmy. Next, craft. I notice the joke about noses, which makes the reveal light and clever even as the trap closes. The strongest word is “pug”: it is a short, funny word, and it is the evidence. Then, effect. How does this line reveal the truth about the man who arrives? My answer: Bob's own line reveals that the tall man who arrived is not Jimmy Wells, because the noses don't match; the stranger is a plainclothes officer who arrests Bob, and O. Henry hides a sad betrayal inside a joke.

segments.script: Annotate the story for foreshadowing, characterization (three marks with a margin note each), then write one claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph: what does this story suggest about friendship tested by duty? Then start your writing prompt at your assigned level (HS Sophomore: Analyze how After Twenty Years develops the idea of friendship tested by duty. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of irony and foreshadowing shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.) Exemplar: Jimmy proves his loyalty to both his friend and his duty. When the text says “Bob: I was at the appointed place on time” (After Twenty Years, paragraph 33), it shows this directly. His note says "I was at the appointed place on time," so he kept his promise, but he sent another officer because he was bound by duty and could not bear to arrest Bob himself.
